Shared stewardship connections for migratory birds

Source: R/stewardship.R
stewardship_connections.Rd

Generate a shared stewardship connections raster mapping where migratory species that occupy an origin region in one stationary season (breeding/non-breeding) concentrate in the other stationary season (non-breeding/breeding). For each species, the destination-season proportion-of-population raster is multiplied by a species weight (the fraction of the global population in the origin region), and the weighted rasters are summed across all retained species.

Usage

stewardship_connections(
  species = NULL,
  origin_region = NULL,
  region_code = NULL,
  species_weights = NULL,
  origin_season = c("breeding", "nonbreeding"),
  include_migration_seasons = FALSE,
  min_origin_threshold = 1e-04,
  min_migration_threshold = if (include_migration_seasons) 0.5 else 0.85,
  destination_mask = NULL,
  resolution = c("27km", "9km", "3km"),
  filename = NULL,
  path = ebirdst_data_dir(),
  force = FALSE,
  show_progress = interactive(),
  ...
)

Arguments

species

character or NULL; one or more species given as scientific names, common names, or six-letter species codes. Mixes of name types are accepted. The full list of valid species is in ebirdst_runs. In custom polygon mode, species is required. In region-code mode, species optionally subsets the candidate list derived from the regional stats table. In weights-table mode, species optionally subsets the rows of species_weights.

origin_region

NULL, sf, or SpatVector; polygon defining the focal origin region. Required for polygon mode; must be NULL when region_code or species_weights is supplied. If multiple features are present, they are unioned to a single polygon.

region_code

character or NULL; a region code matching one present in ebirdst_regional_stats() (e.g. "USA", "USA-NY", "TWN"). Required for region-code mode; must be NULL otherwise. Use ebirdst_regional_stats() to browse valid codes via the region_code column.

species_weights

data frame or NULL; a data frame with at least two columns: species_code (character, resolved via get_species()) and weight (numeric, finite, non-negative). Required for weights-table mode; must be NULL otherwise. Rows with duplicate resolved species_code values are not permitted. Threshold arguments (min_origin_threshold, min_migration_threshold) and include_migration_seasons are ignored in this mode.

origin_season

character; the stationary season in which the focal region is occupied: "breeding" (default) or "nonbreeding". The destination season is the opposite stationary season.

include_migration_seasons

logical; if TRUE, the weight for each species also considers the fraction of the population within origin_region during the pre- and post-breeding migration seasons (taking the maximum across all origin-season layers present). The default min_migration_threshold is relaxed to 0.5 in this case. Applies only to polygon mode and region-code mode; ignored in weights-table mode. Defaults to FALSE.

min_origin_threshold

numeric [0, 1); minimum weight (fraction of global population in the origin region during origin season(s)) required to retain a species. Species with weight < min_origin_threshold are excluded before the destination-side computation. Applies to polygon mode and region-code mode; ignored in weights-table mode. Defaults to 0.0001 (1%). Set to 0 to disable.

min_migration_threshold

numeric [0, 1); minimum fraction by which a species' population must leave the origin region between the origin and destination stationary seasons. Applies to polygon mode and region-code mode; ignored in weights-table mode. Defaults to 0.85 when include_migration_seasons = FALSE and 0.5 when TRUE. Set to 0 to disable.

destination_mask

NULL, sf, sf, SpatVector, SpatExtent, or a bounding box from sf::st_bbox(); spatial object used to crop and mask the destination-season raster for each species before accumulation. If NULL, the full global raster is used — a destination_mask is strongly recommended for broadly distributed species to reduce memory and compute.

resolution

character; resolution of the raster data: "27km" (default), "9km", or "3km". Note that the example dataset only provides 27 km data. If more than 25 species are requested at finer-than-27km resolution, or more than 100 at 27km, a message is issued about expected download size and compute time.

filename

character or NULL; file path to write the connection raster to disk via terra::writeRaster(). If NULL (default), the raster is returned in memory only. When filename is supplied the return value is invisible and additional arguments in ... are passed to terra::writeRaster().

path

character; directory to download the data to. All downloaded files will be placed in a sub-directory of this directory named for the data version year, e.g. "2020" for the 2020 Status Data Products. Each species' data package will then appear in a directory named with the eBird species code. Defaults to a persistent data directory, which can be found by calling ebirdst_data_dir().

force

logical; if the data have already been downloaded, should a fresh copy be downloaded anyway.

show_progress

logical; whether to print download progress information. Defaults to interactive(), so downloads are silent in non-interactive sessions (e.g. scripts and R Markdown).

...

additional arguments passed to terra::writeRaster() when filename is supplied.

Value

A named list with two elements:

  • connection: a single-layer SpatRaster giving the stewardship connection surface — the weighted sum of destination-season proportion-of-population rasters, with each species weighted by the fraction of its global population in the origin region.

  • weights: a data frame with one row per retained species and columns:

    • species_code: the alphanumeric eBird species code.

    • common_name: the English common name.

    • origin_season: which origin-season produced the proportion of population NA in weights-table mode.

    • weight: fraction of global population in the origin region during the origin season(s). In region-code mode this is total_pop_percent from ebirdst_regional_stats(); in weights-table mode it is the user-supplied value.

    • rel_pct_decrease: fraction of the origin-season proportion of population that left the region by the destination season. NA in weights-table mode.

Details

Input modes: The species and weights can be defined in three quite distinct ways depending on whether region_code, species_weights, or origin_region is supplied:

  • Region-code mode (region_code): provide a region code (e.g. "USA", "USA-NY") matching one present in ebirdst_regional_stats(). The candidate species list is derived automatically from that region; species optionally subsets it. Weights and thresholds are derived from total_pop_percent in the regional stats table — no proportion-of-population rasters are downloaded for filtered-out species.

  • Custom polygon mode (origin_region): provide an sf or SpatVector polygon defining the focal origin region. In this mode, a set of species must be supplied via the species argument. For each species the weight and inclusion thresholds are computed by calculating the seasonal proportion-of-population within the supplied polygon.

  • Weights-table mode (species_weights): provide a data frame with columns species_code and weight (numeric, non-negative). Weights are used as supplied; threshold arguments and include_migration_seasons are ignored. species optionally subsets the rows.

Species selection note: There is significant download and compute cost for processing large numbers of species. For the custom polygon mode, the typical workflow is to use ebirdst_regional_stats(), or other datasets, to coarsely subset the species list before calling this function. Region-code mode does this subsetting automatically.

This method was developed by the Cornell Lab of Ornithology and Partners in Flight (PIF). The approach is described in:

  • Partners in Flight (2023). Making Connections for Bird Conservation, 2nd Edition. PIF Technical Series No. 10. https://partnersinflight.org/resources/pif-technical-series-10-making-connections-appendices-and-maps/

  • Lello-Smith et al. (2026). Biological Conservation 313: 111551. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.biocon.2025.111551

Important: The resulting raster shows multispecies abundance concentrations weighted by origin-region population representation — it is not a migratory connectivity metric. The individuals present in the destination season are not necessarily the same individuals that occupy the focal region in the origin season.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Appalachian warblers with breeding populations in West Virginia
warblers <- c("cerwar", "woewar1", "louwat", "buwwar", "hoowar")

# West Virginia: rough bounding box in WGS84
origin_region <- sf::st_sf(geometry = sf::st_as_sfc(
  sf::st_bbox(
    c(xmin = -82.6, xmax = -77.7, ymin = 37.2, ymax = 40.6),
    crs = sf::st_crs(4326)
  )
))

# Central America destination mask (Central Mexico through Panama)
destination_mask <- sf::st_bbox(
    c(xmin = -99, xmax = -80, ymin = 10, ymax = 22),
    crs = sf::st_crs(4326)
)

# region-code mode: weights from ebirdst_regional_stats()
result_rc <- stewardship_connections(
  warblers,
  region_code = "USA-WV",
  origin_season = "breeding",
  destination_mask = destination_mask,
  resolution = "27km"
)
result_rc$weights

# polygon mode: weights derived from proportion-population rasters
result_poly <- stewardship_connections(
  warblers,
  origin_region = origin_region,
  origin_season = "breeding",
  destination_mask = destination_mask,
  resolution = "27km"
)
result_poly$weights

# weights-table mode: supply weights directly, skips threshold filtering
wt <- data.frame(
  species_code = warblers,
  weight = c(0.12, 0.08, 0.15, 0.20, 0.10)
)
result_wt <- stewardship_connections(
  species_weights = wt,
  origin_season = "breeding",
  destination_mask = destination_mask,
  resolution = "27km"
)

# display the connection surface
brks <- importance_breaks(result_poly$connection)
pal <- c("#e6e6e6", ebirdst_palettes(length(brks) - 2))
terra::plot(
  result_poly$connection,
  breaks = brks,
  col = pal,
  axes = FALSE,
  box = TRUE,
  legend = FALSE,
  mar = c(0.25, 0.25, 0.25, 0.25)
)
} # }
